sentences.text:
Gagan Singh Rajput vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27
February, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Jbp:17381
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Sandeep N. Bhatt
 On The 27th Of February, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 10095 of 2026

Gagan Singh Rajput
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Rajendra Kumar Gupta - Advocate for the applic
 Shri Swatantra Pandya - P.L. for State.

Order 
This is third repeat application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.61/2022 registered at Police Station - Mahila Thana, Jabalpur, District - Jabalpur (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2), 420, 109, 112, 114, 120(B) of IPC.

Applicant is in detention since 24.07.2025.
2.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that this is third bail application and charge-sheet has been filed and material witnesses were examined and they are also not supporting the case of the prosecution.

Moreover, it is submitted that the applicant is 30 years of old and the complainant,
who is widow, is 40 years of old.
It is further submitted that the medical examination also does not disclose any offence regarding rape.

The complainant filed the complaint after delay of more than six months and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:17381 2 MCRC-10095-2026 the report as well as complainant's statement do not specify anything about the incident of rape.
The applicant is behind the Bar since 24.07.2025 and there is no antecedents against the applicant and trial will take some more time to its conclusion, therefore, the applicant be released on bail.
3. Per contra, counsel for the State has opposed the application and prays for rejection of the bail application.

It is further submitted by him that there is statements under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
which prima facie establish the involvement of the present applicant in the crime in question.
He has submitted that since the trial is going on and will be concluded within short period, no discretion should be exercised.

4. Heard the submissions and perused the case diary.

sentences.text: After disposal of the earlier bail application, further deposition of the some witnesses were recorded, who are material witnesses for the prosecution.
The FIR is filed after delay of six months and there is no material available by way of medical evidence which indicates about the element of the rape.
The applicant is 30 years old whereas the victim is aged about 40 years.
Prima facie it seems that there is some consensual relationship and thereafter there is some dispute.

The applicant is in custody since 23.09.2025 coupled with the fact that trial will take a considerable time as well as the principle 'bail is the rule and jail is the exception' as well as Article 21 of the Constitution of India and the material witnesses were examined, but without expressing any view on the merits of the case, I deem it a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, the application is allowed.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:17381 3 MCRC-10095-2026 6 .

It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court,
for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial and shall co-operate in trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
